<thought>We have the molecular ion at m/z ≈ 121 Da, a carbonyl carbon at ~168 ppm and six aromatic carbons (≈127–134 ppm) in the ¹³C NMR, indicating a benzene ring bearing a carbonyl substituent (likely an ester or acid). The neutral mass of 121 Da fits C₇H₅O₂ (M = 121 Da). This formula corresponds to benzoic acid missing one hydrogen (i.e., the deprotonated anion) or, more plausibly, to phenyl formate (C₇H₆O₂, M = 122 Da) whose [M]⁺ would appear at 122 Da, not 121. To resolve the ambiguity we need the ¹H NMR spectrum to see the number and type of protons (e.g., aromatic pattern, presence of an aldehydic or formyl proton).</thought>
